answer: Honest-anchored trust propagation with decay-per-hop resists sybils: trust spreads from the honest seed losing a fixed fraction each hop, so identities many hops from the seed inherit almost nothing. A sparrow-light sybil cluster reachable only through a long chain of attack edges receives trust attenuated to near-zero; the vertex of trust sits at the seed and fades with distance. A wander of fakes far from the honest core cannot amplify their inherited trust internally — propagation only ever decays outward, so remoteness from honest ground caps a whole cluster's standing.
